CASE-0808.canonical: I arrived at the store and consulted with the manager. I proceeded to identify the unit, which had fans running but the compressor was off. I began the diagnosis and found the Carell control unit damaged. The display indicated that the refrigeration was working, but there was no signal. I went to several supply stores but couldn't find a replacement, so I adapted a Dixell control unit. DNI ,After the adaptation, the magnetic contactor was found to be damaged. I returned to the supply store, and it was installed and restarted. The temperature began to decrease, the setpoint was adjusted, and it is now working correctly.

CASE-0809.canonical: The mini split in the AP office was leaking water from the insulation on the suction line.

CASE-0810.canonical: I pulled the covers off the evaporator to check the EEV screens because the txv on the condenser was clogged. I pulled the screens on both eevs and they were both completely clogged I used some parts cleaner to clean off all the junk and clear the screens up. I also noticed some oil around the transducer king valve I pulled the caps off and noticed the valve core was leaking so I swapped the valve core out with a new one no more leaks. Also reattached a electrical cover inside the walk in that had fallen off. Drained the line, removed drain insulation, poured water down the drain, and a tiny water leak started coming out of the front access port fitting. This part of the drain line was not replaced, and the leak may have been caused by a stress fracture while the new line was installed. Cleared all water from out of the drain line, dried the area, sanded it down and welded the small open hole with flux and soft solder. Poured water down the drain again, and leak was now sealed. Re-insulated drain line with existing insulation and insulation tape.

0D1B2E2C-7A76-4D07-B312-000FD43E5C65.text: The liquid line solenoid was not opening. Bad coil. We used a magnet to get it open. That led us to another thought. The leak we found was not big enough to have lost that amount of refrigerant in a short period of time. So we looked at the relief and high pressure safety. The plastic cap that someone had previously placed on the relief had the center blown out. We checked the auto reset high pressure safety. It was set at 450 psi... the same pressure the relief is rated at. At this point we believe the solenoid failed and caused the valve to stay closed. The compressor pumped against a closed solenoid and built up enough pressure to blow the relief. Then it shut the system off and the pressures dropped. The system repeated this process until the low pressure safety did not allow the system to run. Then refrigerant was slowly leaking out of the core assembly.

The only issue I found was with the evaporator condensate pan is full of water and float is bad. Unit will need a new evaporator condensate pan. I pin pointed the smell to the condenser fan motor but it tested good and is operating within spec. There is oil leaking from motor casing. This fan motor will need to be replaced. I inspected all wiring underneath case and found no issues. I inspected all evaporator fan motors and wiring and found no issues there. Compressor is running and pulling 5.7 amps. Will submit bid to replace parts. As of now unit is running and cycling on temp of 32°f. Found the float was sticking causing unit to over amp and trip the breaker. The condensate heater was the main culprit and the overflowing water from the pan caused more issues. I Started removing as much water as I could to prevent some of the mess that was made. Once I was able to get the rusted screws out I was then able to remove and replace the condensate pan. There is no plug so I ran wires back to the specific junction box and hard wired the new connections in. At this time case is down to temp and no other issues found.

I used some self tapping screws and remounted the coil temp sensor so that the fans would come on sooner and the T1 case won’t get behind.

Was able to locate a new fuse holder and fuse at the Hoshizaki distribution warehouse, ran and grabbed the parts needed. On return I installed new connectors onto wiring and installed new fuse and holder. Kept motor unplugged and turned unit on to test voltage to the harness. After a long delay and no motor voltage, I noticed that the infrared eye for bin level had both lights on, pulled it out and found nearly all the way blocked. Cleaned it off and left it out for testing. Turned unit back on Voltage was correct, turned unit off and plugged the motor back in and out my amp clamp on, turned unit on. Motor runs normal, before freeze cycle it’s running 2.5-3.0 amps, when freeze cycle starts it topped out 4.5-5.0 amps. After running continuously for around a hour, highest amp draw I seen was 5.7amp.

4F8191AE-47DD-4B5F-8CDE-6DF690F7B2FB.text: During the inspection, standing water was observed beneath the case; however, the source of the leak was not immediately visible. I poured water into the drain system while observing underneath the case with a flashlight and traced the drain piping to the floor drain. Further investigation revealed that two separate condensate drain lines were routed into the same floor drain opening. During the original installation, two 90-degree elbows had been cut and positioned directly against one another at the drain entrance. This configuration caused condensate from one drain line to overflow onto the adjacent drain fitting, allowing water to spill onto the floor and migrate beneath the display case.

FEF92C81-AB80-4E7A-8560-77DFE5A497C0.text: Found pan full of water. Covered product below the evaporator, disconnected drain union, and confirmed the evaporator drain line was restricted and preventing proper drainage. Cleared drain line with nitrogen and verified water began draining into the primary drain system. Drainage remained significantly slow and the pan continued holding water, indicating a larger restriction downstream primary drain system. Traced the line exiting both coolers and terminating at a sink located in the warehouse hallway. Observed only minimal drainage at the sink despite the evaporator pan holding and overflowing with water, confirming a restriction within the shared primary drain line. Accessing CLR 4 Evaporator 3-A and opened the cleanout fitting located at the high point of the primary drain line. Found significant slime and organic buildup inside the drain piping. Began clearing the system with nitrogen through the cleanout and coordinated with warehouse associates to move pallets and gain access to the remaining evaporators. After treatment completed, slowly opened cleanout and observed a significant amount of water, slime, and debris discharge from the drain line, confirming blockage breakdown.

90520E2E-1F05-4600-853E-F76124F99FC9.text: The E2 for rack A was blank no power. Check incoming voltage to the rack and had no voltage. Check main breaker , it was a 400 amp breaker. Was trip, I reset breaker. Before powering up the rack. I check if any compressors were short to ground. All check out good, check and inspect any loose wire or burn wire . All check out good, then I power up each compressor toggle switch on and compressors started staging up . Rack ran about 35-45 minutes and breaker trip again. I then visual inspection all pecker heads from the compressors and they were dry no condensation. Reset breaker and rack stay on much longer. Check breaker temperature and it was 40° hotter than rack B. The toggle had a lot of play. Call Steve and he will call an electrician to look at the 400 amp main breaker. Will leave call open to come back and inspect again. Rack is on and temperatures are dropping for know. Check out with manager Anthony. Electricians on sight once I arrived . They took a look at the main breaker rated at 400 amps . Breaker reset and system online . I watched for any arcing issues on the compressors . All remain online . Was called and told that the electrician will quote out a new breaker due to possible issues with the breaker itself.

I screwed it back together. Case now has good air flow. The reason the mullion heaters weren’t working is because the case is iced up. At the top of the case is a there is a high limit and if the case is to warm it shuts the mullion heaters off. Ice buildup in doors is gone but circuit B12 is all frozen solid and has no airflow. Ran unit through multiple defrosts to clear coil. The issue with the freezer is that suction pressure is at 6psi and can only maintain 0°.

We need to come up with a way so that we could either take the freezer down or completely deice that section we need to deice both evaporators and both in caps at the exact same time so that we can use water but we need somewhere to put the product most likely a refer trailer. We will also need to get with the facility and with us to come up with the best possible time that we can do the repair so that we could take the freezer down at one time.

ACE62336-C65F-4DC0-BD44-636238168D33.text: Compressor 1 was locked out on oil pressure fail and liquid level was at 0%. I acknowledged all the alarms, reset compressor 1, power cycled the Rack, once it started up and running, I watched the liquid line site glass, found it flashing and still reading 0% on E2, but left it running while I leak checked the store, the Rack and the condensers, no leak found. With the rack being down for that long and all the EPR valves wide open, liquid migrated and piled up either in cases, float circuit or condenser, valved off the liquid line just past site glass and watched liquid level on E2. Once the level got to around 35% I opened the valve back up. I’m looking at the liquid level log, it appears that it was hitting some pretty high levels up to 100% just prior to the rack shutting down. Compressor 3 was overridden awaiting repairs and compressor 1&2 locked out on oil failure. The oil separator/reservoir had two balls floating indicating enough oil into the system. The net oil pressure of compressor 1 and 2 arranged between 50 to 60 psi, which is relatively high, even though the section pressure has not reached setpoint.

B11DC9BE-FBEC-4C18-9957-38F011B64AEE.text: Found the compressor fuses blown. Troubleshot the unit and found the compressor fuses blown. Found blown fuse, shut down unit and checked if comp was grounded which it wasn’t, checked comp windings which all matched up and were reading good, checked ohms across comp contactor and checked if it was grounded which it wasn’t, pulled apart comp contactors and noticed contactor was pretty hot and starting to char up inside, wiped down contactor and replaced bad fuse with one spare inside panel, kicked on unit and let it run, checked to see if any voltage drop across contactor and found L1 starting to have voltage drop of 1.3V, noticed comp amps running around 16-17A with a max operating amp rated for 25A, comp could be intermittently starting to lock up and blowing fuse let unit run and monitored amps, started checking voltage and noticed that incoming voltage drops low to around 196-197V on the incoming feed to the RCU which could play a factor, recommend rebuilding comp contactor and re check comp amperage, if amps still trending high, recommend replacement before rotor fully locks up.

Drained sump until fill solenoid energized and started filling to confirm operation. Pulled sensor bundle in the sump and cleaned. Seer2 Informed me that the alarm has been fairly constant over the last couple months but clears after less than a minute.

Found compressor 6 off on oil. Reset and compressor came online. Checked and compressor was pulling 20 amps. Checked oil reservoir and found it empty. Added 1 gallon Poe to bring level up to 1 ball. Got fan running. Ran hose to roof to get Rack running. Motor type. 1 1/2 hp see pictures. Found the two condenser fan motors out on A Rack. Searched the store for the motors, and could not find them. Read notes and tried to pick up at another store, correct fan motors were not at that store either, someone dropped motor back off at 748, returned to store and removed old condenser fan motors on rack and installed to, checked voltage and amps , 200v pulling 5.3 amps. Checked rack A discharge pressure and found at 200 psig.

CD593CC9-A473-435C-87DE-A752AE601B6C.text: I arrived at the store and checked in with MIC. We walked receiving and the training room and it was noticeably warmer than the last time I was at the store. Checked the BX and found the heat is always being called for. Space temp was 69° dewpoint was 53° return air temp was 66°, mixed air was 70°, and supply temp was 81°. Outside temperature was 86°. There was no stages of cooling being called for. Graphed cooling stages. Stages and 1 and 2 have not been on since yesterday and stage 3 has not been called for as far back as log goes. Checked the calibration of the sensors and they were accurate. Checked the RTU and noticed the OSA damper was almost all the way open. Adjusted the stopper for the actuator so the damper would not open all the way. When two stages of cooling was called for stage 2 was not running. When I opened the electrical cover of the compressor stage 2 came on. Went through wiring and found a loose wire on the splice connection for the LPS. Fixed the wiring and the compressor stayed running. The BX stopped calling for heat but the supply temp was still warm. Checked racks 5 and 6 and found the heat reclaim was still on for rack 6 but not being called for. The dip switch for the output was in the wrong position. Set the dip switch then checked the supply temp. It’s now 55° and dropping. The receiving and training room are now cooling down. There’s no other issues at this time.

F58EEF56-EF3E-40B3-B9E1-3242D4B48840.text: With all possible issues checked for both systems only possible cause for high temperature Alarm is low CO2 level. Made my way to CO2 pump rack and checked receiver sight glass and found very low CO2 liquid level.

C8712523-A793-4C78-B121-84A33985010B.text: Discovered multiple incorrect operating parameters. Found P-01 Cut In Temperature set to 32°F and P-02 Cut Out Differential set to 3F, resulting in the case energizing refrigeration at approximately 32F and satisfying at approximately 29F, causing the case to operate excessively cold and contributing to ice accumulation. Also discovered P-56 EEV Start Opening was set to 100%, causing aggressive refrigerant feeding during startup. Returned P-56 to factory setting of 10% opening and adjusted temperature control parameters back to proper medium temperature operating values.

52D45E14-F779-46EC-9842-B9DDFEAFC3F3.text: Compressor B8 in proof alarms locked out on High pressure safety.  Reset,  overrode on verified operations.  Noted abnormal faint sound and vibration every now and then, switch off sound went away switched cycled eventually comp went off on High pressure safety.  On start up again.  Isolated and pumped down comp, removed discharge  service valve.  Found pieces of discharge valve (compressor parts)  in port, replaced gaskets and re installed valve.  Compressor will need to be replaced.

DF317789-E977-4BDB-92B3-6F61971AC23C.text: Found condenser fans to be running but not compressor. Located contactor and was pulled in but compressor not pulling amps. Checked load side and one leg was pulling 50 while others was pulling 208-230 and compressor was single phasing due to contactor. Went ahead and de energized condenser. Removed old contactor and found it to have arched on inside of contactor. Installed new contactor. Checked windings and verified compressor was not going to ground. Ohmed all three legs and all were good. Went ahead and energized condenser and compressor energized. Checked running amps and found 2 of the 3 legs to be overamping compared to others. Let compressor run and amps dropped down below FLA. Both legs still was borderline and was probably damaged due to single phase occurring when contactor was single phasing. Checked compressor and found it to be running hotter than usual. Let condenser continue to run to get cases back down to setpoint. Let MIC know of issue and to light stock cases due to compressor is going out. Will call supply houses to get new compressor on order and in route and return to install.

Electric is shut down and marked. Cases have dropped to sent points or very close. 1 alarm for inverter after disconnect for vfd was shut down.

Performed a pump down test, after turning off compressor pressures went up to discharge pressure which was 178 on the suction side. Had valved compressor completely off and when we opened the discharge service valve it got to 80 psi right away. Could feel end bell of compressor getting warm when suction service valve was shut and compressor was off. Compressor is now isolated, we turned off toggle switch and switchgear for the VFD that runs with Compressor 10-A. There is an inverter alarm because we turned it off. We acknowledged and muted alarm, need to override. Case temps are back down to normal with Compressor isolated.

AB36C22F-49B3-40A8-B61E-853C43E8EB68.text: I checked in using the third-party app and completed the on-site MIC check-in. I then proceeded to the sales floor and located the multi-deck refrigeration system. The case temperature was elevated, with the case temperature at 42°F. I began troubleshooting System #7 and found that the unit was locked out on a high-discharge-pressure safety trip. I checked the discharge pressure and found it operating at approximately 330 PSI. I then verified the discharge pressure safety control and found it set to cut out at 400 PSI. Next, I inspected the condenser coil and found no visible obstructions; however, the condenser fins were damaged in several areas. I also checked the liquid line filter drier for any signs of restriction and found none. After power-cycling the controller to restart the system, the unit tripped again on high discharge pressure. I then performed a thorough cleaning of the condenser coil until the rinse water ran clear. Once cleaning was completed, I restarted the system and monitored operation. After cleaning, the system operated normally and did not trip on high discharge pressure.

Found that rack 2 had all of the compressors tripped on oil which caused all compressors to trip on oil which caused rack 1 to shut down. Once all compressors on rack 2 were operating rack 1 then began to start up. We then monitored rack until both racks were fully operating. We then began troubleshooting what caused rack to flood out. Noticed pan was very dirty, unscrewed pan off evap coil and took pan all the way off and brought to janitor sink to clean with hot water. Cleaned drain line as best I could. Screwed pan back onto evap coil tested pan with water and water was draining.

A506ECCF-A246-46E5-98EF-3FB9BEACD0C4.text: Found the two cases evaporator partially iced up due to case settings.

DF4657E0-20F3-42C1-8BDB-B7740775FCEC.text: Found leak at compressor suction service valve.

Esc no good, compressor 3 on medium temp rack is no good, removed esc and installed on low temp rack for compressor 3.

0BA7B743-E0BC-48F7-874F-5C6BF25DAEC0.text: I picked up the rebuild kits and leak-checked the hot gas valves to identify which ones were leaking, confirming issues on two valves.

C7374CA1-25E9-4ABE-AA99-CA7758C3AFF4.text: Adjusted setpoints for units as they were set for winter settings. Store now running around 70°

C2D89354-8561-4DC7-A163-A36F1AA6C37E.text: Performed a leak check and Found 9999 PPMs behind compressor #2 and Repaired leak on site .

Condenser 10 with all fan motors and compressors not running; resetting the controller breaker restored operation, and shortly afterward the high-discharge and case over-temp alarms cleared. One compressor on the right side short-cycling even though the space temperature was at setpoint; a follow-up visit is recommended to evaluate the unit further.

Found wire going from contactor to fuses for motors shorted and burnt out that landed on T2. Re did connection for bottom of contactor and checked all safety’s. Fan cycle and AT closed. Turned unit back on and found fans now running. Will need to return to replace wire going from contactor to fuses and replace contactor.

4655B13C-F328-4AF3-83A4-55DDAC5633B7.text: Found Walmart Tech Harrison on-site with Rack C down..Harry had found a line break and had leak isolated and had picked up gas.Added 400# to rack and staged rack back on..more gas was needed..after Harrison repaired leak he ran for more gas..and dropped off gas and left..pulled vacuum on C5 and verified leak repair..Staged Rack back on 100% and added 200 more to obtain 25% receiver level under full load..conducted additional leak check..no other leaks detected..all Rack C circuits all set point and all Rack ops normal..Gave Evan defrost schedules..and checked out..call complete

74D89020-B4EF-4350-ACF7-3C6174D7A291.text: Found blown control fuse and traced issue to bad contactor coil, replaced contactor and system no up and running.

B83A2EDB-1527-4352-9E78-F06BA69A7781.text: I found that all three units were tripped. I power cycled the units restoring power to the units. I found the KE2 controllers reading warm. I headed inside the freezer to confirm that the evaporator coils were not iced up and that the fans are spinning. I then headed to the roof to look at the RCUs. I found that all three units were tripped. I power cycled the units restoring power to the units. After confirming that the units turned on I headed back in the store. I monitored the temperature of the units and found that the temperature began to drop. The systems are currently at temp and maintaining. I let the manager know. Checked in with overnight coach Clayvon R. Located unit OGP 5,6, walk in freezer. OGP 4, walk in cooler over temping upon arrival. Acces roof hatch run assessments diagnosed units down on IT software boards offline. Got units back online monitored temps and walked boxes with coach.

A65AF433-FC3C-48D6-939B-D77692ED066E.text: Seen drain clogged with slimy algae. Vacuumed it out and vacuumed the Ptrap out. Used to two cartridges of CO2 to clear the drain line. Water then started flowing.

8F0D41A2-2383-4E94-A8D0-91C1C937B337.text: Then it went into a defrost mode and allowed it to finished the defrost and then finished thawing it with my little hand torch. Put the racks back in it and turned it back on. Cleaned out my work area. Let it run for a while and then checked it again. Temperature at 20*f now and dropping. With good airflow inside.

D1D39EE1-B3BD-4465-9C4A-655C1144CC96.text: The motor is dead, we will need to order a new motor and a new plug in dial for the ecm motor- Must be the greenheck motor that I list.

Walked the store and checked for leaks did not find any. Recommend someone come back and do a follow up the rack and check the charge and check for more leaks. Also noticed a fan not working in the walk in freezer. Added five full drums of 404A and one partial that was 16 pounds. Found two leaks on two separate solenoids on the liquid lines. Case number 11 will need a new TXV valve pumped the system down and tried removing the screen which was seized onto the TXV valve could not adjust the valve either so we’ll need to order a new DXV valve for that case information on the valve is in pictures

Tapped on the relay and this closed the switch. Discovered some loose wiring on the output 14 circuit. Tightened connections.

7579EAE9-2D89-4AFA-906C-F961E3FBE514.text: She said all controller are pinging and have good data.

3F6FADD3-6607-4FB0-B6E9-0C68913DD995.text: Found LT comp 2 off in oil safety. Reset safety and monitored operation. Checked and confirmed good oil pressure 48 psi.

52F2EE32-4712-4205-A532-EE37F293BE16.text: Power cycled the e2 but still reading offline.

6A8F3150-1D22-4960-BD85-E3AD3FC35742.text: Found no voltage at fans and coil power on fan relay which was holding out NC fan contact. Traced issue back to failed 34yr old fan Klixon.

BC582524-7EEB-4C3C-AEB0-D400100D2656.text: observe compressor short cycling and see that condenser fan motor is attempting to spend but failing to do so

282FA8B9-676D-4C9E-8CF1-ED90094292E6.text: replaced all of the gaskets on the deli lowboy, screw style

Called digital asset level 1 and spent significant time on the phone with them, got transferred to level 3 and they stated that Walmart techs were working on this earlier (Friday afternoon) and they are the ones who left it in test, they changed the board and several components.

5E88B201-A8E1-439F-AED7-9F506A9D3E73.text: Found thermometer on cooler with the bulb snapped off of the capillary tube and unable to read temperature.

Removed insulation on liquid line. 9999ppm Leak was on a coupling between the rack & the ball valves for the Evap banks in the freezer where there was a pinhole gap in the solder. Confirmed leak with soap bubbles.

304D242C-E8A3-4CCB-8CE1-C4D80AF5C10D.text: Found fan motor running intermittently. Cut power to fan motor and verified 120v, motor no good.

7A10DD49-C7A0-4409-A687-47883770F527.text: I then went to rack and noticed EEV superheat at 18. I then reset and monitored. Both EEVs are now at 11 degrees superheat and operating properly.

30C9A39E-10D3-4944-A8EA-9896BBC8EDC3.text: Compressor is sporadically losing oil pressure.

Checked coils, clean. Checked refrigerant site glass after a few mins. Site glass clear. Went back down into WIF and checked the evaporator fan settings. Changed the fan control so the fans would run at normal speed not slow.

I also noticed some oil around the transducer king valve I pulled the caps off and noticed the valve core was leaking so I swapped the valve core out with a new one no more leaks. Also reattached a electrical cover inside the walk in that had fallen off. Drained the line, removed drain insulation, poured water down the drain, and a tiny water leak started coming out of the front access port fitting. This part of the drain line was not replaced, and the leak may have been caused by a stress fracture while the new line was installed. Cleared all water from out of the drain line, dried the area, sanded it down and welded the small open hole with flux and soft solder. Poured water down the drain again, and leak was now sealed. Re-insulated drain line with existing insulation and insulation tape.
